outline.chapter_title: Introduction: The Case for Tokenizer-Free Language Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the fundamental limitations of current tokenization-based Large Language Models (LLMs), such as sensitivity to noise, lack of orthographic knowledge, and multilingual inequity. It motivates the need for byte-level modeling and presents the core thesis of the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT): matching token-based performance while improving efficiency through dynamic compute allocation.
subtopics: The Role and Limitations of Static Tokenization (BPE)
Challenges in Scaling Raw Byte-Level Models
The Core Idea: Dynamic Compute Allocation via Patching
Overview of BLT Contributions and Performance Claims
Comparison Goals: Parity with Llama 3 and Inference Efficiency

outline.chapter_title: Patching Strategies: From Fixed Strides to Entropy-Based Segmentation
outline.description: This chapter details the mechanism of 'patching'—grouping bytes into variable-sized units for processing. It critically evaluates different segmentation strategies, culminating in the novel entropy-based patching method that drives BLT's efficiency by aligning compute usage with data complexity.
subtopics: Defining Patches vs. Tokens: Vocabulary Independence
Static Patching: Strided Approaches and Their Downsides
Heuristic Patching: Space-Based Segmentation
Dynamic Patching: Estimating Next-Byte Entropy
Algorithms for Boundary Detection: Global Thresholds vs. Approximate Monotonicity
Incremental Patching Requirements for Autoregressive Generation

outline.chapter_title: The BLT Architecture: A Hierarchical Design
outline.description: A deep dive into the structural components of the Byte Latent Transformer. This chapter explains how BLT separates concerns between local byte processing and global latent reasoning using a three-part architecture: a Local Encoder, a Global Latent Transformer, and a Local Decoder.
subtopics: High-Level Architectural Overview
The Local Encoder: Mapping Bytes to Latent Patches
Enhancing Representations with Hash N-Gram Embeddings
Cross-Attention Mechanisms: Pooling Bytes into Patch Representations
The Global Latent Transformer: Autoregressive Reasoning on Patches
The Local Decoder: Reconstructing Bytes from Latents
Masking Strategies and Positional Encodings

outline.description: This chapter focuses on the mathematical formulation of computational cost (FLOPs) in BLT compared to traditional models. It presents empirical scaling laws, demonstrating how BLT achieves compute-optimal training and superior inference-time scaling by manipulating patch sizes.
subtopics: FLOPs Estimation Framework for Hybrid Architectures
Bits-Per-Byte (BPB) as a Tokenizer-Independent Metric
Compute-Optimal Training Regimes: BLT vs. BPE Baselines
Fixed-Inference Budget Scaling: Growing Model Size via Larger Patches
The Trade-off Between Patch Size, Sequence Length, and Model Capacity
Empirical Results: Crossing Over Traditional Scaling Curves
